body:
Followup to https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/33320

Problem:
- Explicit `:bcd` (etc.) persists from `nvim_buf_call()` but not from an
  autocmd handler targeting a hidden buf (`LspAttach`, `TermRequest`, …),
  which needs a `vim.schedule()` workaround.
- `vim._with()` is supposed to work as a "sandbox", discarding
  side-effects, but it leaks CWD changes: `:lcd` from a `win` context,
  any chdir from a visible-buffer context.

Solution:
- Explicit :cd/:tcd/:bcd during a temp context persists by default.
  - "Ambient" directory changes ('autochdir', existing win-local CWD,
    etc.) are still undone, as before.
- Add `kCtxKeepDirs`: snapshot/restore the target's full CWD state
  (w/b/tp-local, global, cwd). Used by `vim._with{keepcwd}`
  and `'inccommand'`, which must not leak state.

comment_data.body: after this PR, `vim._with` will always restore CWD for all scopes. This seems to match the intended goal of `vim._with`, WDYT @echasnovski ?
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -1533,9 +1533,13 @@ local get_context_state = function(context)
   return res
 end
 
---- Executes function `f` with the given context specification.
+--- Executes function `f` with the given `context` spec: after execution, the original state
+--- indicated by the spec is restored.
 ---
 --- Notes:
+--- - If `buf`/`win` is specified, CWD state (win/buf/tab-local dirs) is restored after execution.
+---   Any :cd/:tcd/:lcd/:bcd during execution is undone.
+---   - TODO: allow opt-out? Workaround: use nvim_buf_call()/nvim_win_call().

comment_data.body: although `kCtxKeepDirs` (and the `vim._with` change) is not strictly necessary for the original goal of this PR (which was to allow `:bcd` in an autocmd to work, even on hidden buffers), I decided to figure out the full story here because it was starting to sprout special cases.
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -45,15 +45,22 @@ typedef struct {
 
 /// Flags for ctx_switch().
 typedef enum {
+  /// Restore process CWD: undo incidental chdir ('autochdir', "leaked" win/tab-local CWD).
+  ///
+  /// Note: this flag only exists for performance. Semantically every ctx-switch wants this, but the
+  /// getcwd() bookkeeping is costly for internal switches that don't run user code.
+  kCtxKeepCwd = 1,
+  /// Restore the target's full CWD state: undo all "chdir" operations on ctx_restore(), including
+  /// explicit :cd/:tcd/:bcd (which otherwise persist).
+  /// - Note: :lcd targeting a hidden buffer (temp window) is always discarded.
+  kCtxKeepDirs = 2,

> after this PR, `vim._with` will always restore CWD for all scopes. This seems to match the intended goal of `vim._with`, WDYT @echasnovski ?

I think the idea of `vim._with` was/is that it restores only those values explicitly supplied in context. Otherwise performing actions with intended side effects inside of `vim._with` callback becomes not quite predictable.

> WDYT about repurposing the `context.cwd` to be a boolean which enables/disables this behavior? so then callers can do `chdir()` and if `cwd=true` then `_with()` will auto-restore the original CWD.

I think the current behavior of `context.cwd` as path is both more intuitive and flexible:
- To preserve (auto-restore) the current directory, use `vim._with({ cwd = vim.fn.getcwd() }, ... )`.
- To allow side effects of changing the current directory, do not supply anything.

comment_data.body:
for "allow side effects", sure, that's easy (and would also be easy with a boolean flag).

 But for "restore the CWD at all scopes", there is no solution for that.
`context.cwd` only supports one scope, but code may do arbitrary things.

also as the code notes, `context.cmd` currently triggers DirChanged...

> But for "restore the CWD at all scopes", there is no solution for that.
> `context.cwd` only supports one scope, but code may do arbitrary things.

I don't think I have a strong opinion about this. My initial reaction is that the boolean `context.cwd` is less intuitive and useful. Also is somewhat not aligned with other context values, since they have "set this value before and restore the current one after" and not "only restore the current one after".

But if it is the only solution to some actual use case problem, then maybe this doesn't matter much. Maybe my reaction is about the context name `cwd` not quite addressing the "preserve current value" part.

> also as the code notes, `context.cmd` currently triggers DirChanged...

I don't see that as the problem though. More like a note about the behavior because I am not really sure which is better: to trigger the event or not. Then same behavior is about the options.

comment_data.body:
> To preserve (auto-restore) the current directory, use `vim._with({ cwd = vim.fn.getcwd() }, ... )`.

That doesn't work (reliably), or is at least clumsy for non-trivial cases, e.g. if the caller is a  `:lcd` window and `f()` does `:tcd`, the restoring `chdir()` silently leaves the tab-local change in place.

I will rework to add `keepcwd` (no change to `cwd`). This aligns (semantically) with keepalt, keepjumps, etc.
